clue.text: Most of the UN okay changing response in present situation

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its tail end, so the last letter of the following word goes
something changing takes a new form, so the letters before it are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut short
taken as written, as fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A diplomat complains that most of the United Nations keeps shifting its stance.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'present situation' is not the current state of affairs but being handed a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying thanks is the polite reply when someone gives you a gift, so it is the usual response on receiving a present.

clue.text: In mess, card out of order, use this instead?

indicators.note: things out of order are not in their proper sequence, so the letters are scrambled
one thing set in another sits inside it, so the scrambled letters go within the word for mess

blocks.note: a hash is a muddle, as in making a hash of it
taken as written, as fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A shopper whose bank card has failed at the till is told to pay another way.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the surface: if your card is out of order, you pay with this instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard cash is notes and coins, the obvious alternative payment when a card will not work.

clue.text: Unlike most things sold in bars, like chocolate

definitions.text: Unlike most things sold in bars, like chocolate

blocks.clueFragment: Unlike most things sold in bars
blocks.note: surface reading: drinks served across a pub counter are mostly beer, wine and spirits
setter's reading: chocolate is also sold in bars, of another kind, and contains no booze

explanation.surface: Something that stands out from the usual drinks on offer in pubs, much as chocolate does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' plays on two senses: pubs, and the slabs chocolate comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes anything containing no alcohol, which is true of chocolate and untrue of most pub drinks.

clue.text: Enemy's scattered – they put up no resistance

indicators.note: scattered things are thrown about in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A routed army whose soldiers flee without fighting back.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men always agree with their superiors and never offer opposition, so they put up no resistance.

clue.text: Supported by leaders of union, picket office next

indicators.note: the leaders of a group are those at the front, so the first letter of each following word is taken

blocks.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A strike action backed by trade union bosses, with the picket line moving on to an office.
explanation.definitionFit: Resting upon something means being held up by it, so the preposition matches 'supported by'.

clue.text: It makes the speaker promise to embrace new ties, for example

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold something within one's arms, so the following letter goes inside

blocks.note: the person speaking refers to themself as me
N is the abbreviation for new
to swear is to vow or promise

explanation.surface: Something that prompts a talker to pledge to take on fresh neckwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker' suggests a sound-alike, but here it simply means the person talking, ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Ties are an example of clothing sold for men, so they fall into the category of menswear.

clue.text: On behalf of area, providing places for discussion

blocks.note: acting for someone is acting on their behalf
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A council acting for a district by setting up public meeting venues.
explanation.definitionFit: Fora is the Latin plural of forum, a place or gathering where matters are debated.

clue.text: Food and water supplier for so long

blocks.note: fare is food and drink provided, as in simple fare
a well is a shaft dug to supply water

explanation.surface: A provider of food and water who has been at it for a remarkably long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For so long' reads as a duration, but 'so long' is the goodbye and 'for' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: So long is an informal goodbye, and farewell is a more formal way of parting.

clue.text: Deity included in supplication that's excessive

definitions.note: read as 'that which is excessive', a noun phrase

indicators.note: something included in another is placed inside it, so the god goes within the request

blocks.note: a plea is an earnest request or supplication
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A prayer that drags a god into it and asks far too much.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an excess or overabundance, which is what 'that which is excessive' describes.

clue.text: Endlessly make health food

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the next word is cut off

blocks.note: a brand is a make of goods, as in a make of car

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep producing wholesome food without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' looks like a verb but is the noun, a manufacturer's label.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran, the husk of cereal grain, is eaten for its fibre and was long promoted as a health food.

clue.text: What those in charge do to allow judge to cover offence retrospectively

indicators.note: looking back in time suggests reading the word for wrongdoing from back to front
to cover something is to go around it, so the word for allow wraps the reversed letters

blocks.note: to admit is to let in or allow
a sin is a moral offence
to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: Officials letting a judge hush up a past crime after the event.
explanation.definitionFit: Managing and running affairs is the job of whoever is in charge, so the verb describes what they do.

clue.text: Fool you finally call in bank in sympathetic way

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter of the preceding word is used
placed in something means set inside it, so the earlier pieces sit within the word for bank

blocks.note: an ass is a foolish person
the final letter of this word
to ring is to call on the telephone
to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: Someone insulted by being told to ring the bank, as if that were kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is the verb, as in bank on, not a building to telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking reassuringly means comforting and calming someone, which is a sympathetic manner.

clue.text: Unusually clean for someone who works with predator

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters take an unexpected order

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A surprisingly tidy person among those who handle dangerous animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A falconer trains and flies hawks and falcons, which are birds of prey, so works with a predator.

clue.text: King I check and prevent from moving

blocks.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
taken as written
to vet is to examine or check

explanation.surface: A chess player declaring check on a king and pinning it in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King' and 'check' suggest a chess move, but they are separate pieces of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To rivet something, or someone's gaze, is to fix it firmly so it cannot shift.

clue.text: Pass line entering English part of church

indicators.note: something entering another goes inside it, so the single letter is placed within the church part

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
an apse is the vaulted recess at a church's east end
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Directions to walk through and join a queue going into an English church.
explanation.definitionFit: When time elapses it passes or goes by, so the verb matches 'pass'.

clue.text: Deposed ruler making call for peace and harmony, initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of each preceding word is used

blocks.note: sh is the hushing call for quiet
the opening letter of each of these two words

explanation.surface: An ousted leader appealing for calm and unity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peace' here means quiet, not the end of war.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shah of Iran was overthrown in 1979, so the title is a famous example of a ruler removed from power.

clue.text: Small pale child good giving ultimate performance

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
wan means pallid or pale
a son is a male child
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A small, sickly but well-behaved child putting on a final show.
explanation.definitionFit: A swansong is a final public appearance, from the legend that swans sing just before dying.

clue.text: Great heat shown in temperature scale, invariably

blocks.note: F stands for Fahrenheit
ever means always, without variation

explanation.surface: A thermometer that always registers scorching readings.
explanation.definitionFit: A fever is a raised body temperature, and figuratively an intense excitement or heat.

clue.text: Supporting wild trees, he takes care of them

indicators.note: wild means unruly and untamed, so the letters that follow run free into a new order

blocks.note: being for something means supporting it
taken as written, as fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A champion of untamed woodland who looks after it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Them' points back to the trees in the wordplay, so the definition leans on the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A forester is employed to manage and tend woodland, so he looks after the trees.

clue.text: Earth, one going round sun? Just the opposite

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so one word wraps the other
this swaps the roles stated before it, so the surrounding word and the enclosed word trade places

blocks.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A question about the Earth orbiting the sun, corrected to its reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the opposite' turns the surface around: the sun goes round one, so the numeral sits inside the Latin name.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth in the lower-case sense is the ground or soil plants grow in.

clue.text: Lack of response from independent Conservative dividing people

indicators.note: something dividing a word splits it apart by sitting in its middle

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for independent
a nation is a people
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: An independent politician and a Tory splitting the public, who shrug.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaction is a failure to act, so it describes an absence of any reaction.

clue.text: Wielder of rod showing irritation about student

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for irritation goes around the single letter

blocks.note: anger is strong annoyance or irritation
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A teacher wielding a cane, cross with a pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: The rod suggests old school punishment, but it is a fishing rod.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler fishes with a rod and line, so he is the person who wields one.

clue.text: Leaves opportunity for rest of the workers, briefly

blocks.note: tea is the dried leaves of the tea plant
a break is a chance, as in a lucky break

explanation.surface: Staff who quit at the chance of a short rest from work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb (goes away) but is the noun for tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea break is a short pause in the working day for a hot drink, a brief rest for workers.

clue.text: Fine service, including baked dish for each person

indicators.note: including means taking in something, so the service word holds the dish inside it

blocks.note: an ace in tennis is an unreturnable serve
a pie is a baked pastry dish

explanation.surface: A restaurant offering good service with a pie for every diner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like waiting at table but is a tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece means each or per head, as in tickets cost five pounds apiece.

clue.text: So captain set out for remote base on round-the-world trip

indicators.note: set out can mean laid out afresh, so the letters before it are arranged differently

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder for the rearrangement
taken as written; this word also serves the indicator

explanation.surface: A captain departs for a distant outpost on a voyage around the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' does double duty, in the fodder and with 'out' as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A space station is a crewed base far from home that continually orbits, travelling round the world.

clue.text: It's a north-facing wine-producing region

indicators.note: in a down clue, facing north means reading upwards, so the words are taken back to front

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A description of a wine area whose slopes look northwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a town and district in Piedmont, northern Italy, famous for its sparkling wine.

clue.text: Showing skill in piece of furniture (apart from first time)

blocks.note: a table is a piece of furniture
T is the abbreviation for time; it is the letter dropped

explanation.surface: A craftsman demonstrating his talent in making a cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means competent or talented, so it describes someone showing skill.

clue.text: It would be not for the first time, a profit like this

indicators.note: the clue says the answer would become the phrase once a lone letter a is placed before it, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: doing something not for the first time is doing it once more
taken as written; it is the letter taken away

explanation.surface: A boast that a profit of this kind has been made before.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it as: 'not for the first time' would be 'a' plus this answer. Put a lone A before the answer and you get the word meaning once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A gain is something earned or acquired, so a profit is a gain.

clue.text: Bearer of terse report from crazy and diabolical situation

blocks.note: nuts is slang for mad
hell is the devil's domain, and any dreadful state

explanation.surface: A messenger delivering a curt account of a mad and dreadful predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: A brief summary is given 'in a nutshell', so the shell figuratively holds the terse report.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom in a nutshell means put very briefly, so the shell is what carries a concise account.

clue.text: Without exception, people held by police very on edge

indicators.note: held by means contained within, so the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: runs from the end of the first word across the second into the third

explanation.surface: Officers who are all extremely nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyone means all people with none left out, so it sums up 'without exception, people'.
